**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize – “Picture of the Year”**

| Year | Winner |
|------|--------|
| **1998** | *Princess Mononoke* (directed by Hayao Miyazaki) |

“Princess Mononoke” earned the prestigious Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year in 1998—making it the very first Ghibli feature to receive that honor.

---

### Box‑office impact & boost to international popularity  

| Aspect | Effect |
|-------|---------|
| **Domestic earnings** | Grossed roughly ¥12 billion (~US$110 million) in Japan alone, becoming the most successful animated film ever released domestically up to that point. |
| **Worldwide reach** | Sold well beyond Japan, eventually earning > US$150 million worldwide. This proved that a fully original, non‑Western story could resonate across cultures. |
| **Distribution leverage** | Success convinced foreign distributors (e.g., Disney/Touchstone, Miramax, Sony Pictures Classics) to acquire rights for theatrical releases in North America, Europe, and Asia. |
| **Critical cachet** | Winning both the national top prize and receiving strong reviews abroad positioned Ghibli as a serious auteur-driven studio rather than just a niche animation house. |
| **Audience growth** | Introduced new viewers to Miyazaki’s world‑building style, paving the way for future hits (“Howl’s Moving Castle,” “Spirited Away”) to secure wide releases and home‑video sales overseas. |
| **Long‑term brand equity** | Established Ghibli as a household name in markets where anime previously had limited mainstream presence, creating a loyal fan community that still drives merchandise, streaming subscriptions, and festival screenings today. |

In short, the combination of record‑breaking domestic revenue and the prestige of winning Japan’s top cinematic accolade gave Studio Ghibli the credibility—and financial muscle—to negotiate larger international distribution agreements, thereby cementing its status as a global cultural icon.
